column1: # The supply chains: the goods the fleet must never run out of, each at its place, with the routes that bring it and
# the division that keeps ships on duty for it (Suggi, 2026-11-17). The store (game/fleet/store.py) reads this file
# into the table supply_chains; its view supply_status sets every chain beside what stands at its place now.
# `supply.py show` (the tool supply) lists them, `supply.py check` is the gate, `supply.py duty` puts the sources of a
# short chain into its keeper's plan (game/fleet/supply.py).
# Kept by the Fleet Admiral with Logistics; a keeper division asks there for a change of its chains.
# Tab-separated; `#` starts a comment; one line per chain, after the header.
# chain          a name of its own: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, once in the file
# item           the item id of the catalog (game/catalog/master-index.md)
# place          where it must stand: `fleet` (anywhere: every station storage and every hold added), a base id of
#                ours (empire/empire.json, bases; a station id of the census works too), a base name, or a system id
#                (every base in it). Faction storage and the fuel bunker are not in the storage book: no reading.
# keep           whole units that must stand there at least: below it the chain is short, below twice it low
# need_per_hour  units used an hour; 0 when not known
# sources        route ids (game/routes/<id>.json) that gather, craft or carry it, with commas; empty when none
# keeper         the division that keeps it on duty: Mining, Trade, Logistics, Military, Intel or Command
# note           why, and what each number rests on

game/reserve.tsv: item station_core 1, one station of our own (plan step P4); kept by the Fleet Admiral with Logistics. No route makes it: the station core foundry does (a facility of the reserve); no route yet.

game/reserve.tsv: keep fuel_cell all, fuel for our own ships beyond the border. The reserve keeps every fuel cell and names no floor: keep 0 until Logistics sets one. No route crafts or buys fuel cells yet.

Iron (catalog: iron_ore, the one iron item; basic_iron_smelting and refine_steel make steel plate of it). keep = the min line of game/reserve.tsv for iron_ore, one figure for one good (requests ENT-355, 2026-11-22: 166,923 here against a reserve demand of 43,040 had the miners' plan follow one of two figures); supply.py check names a difference. Sources: every route file whose floor (min_left) names iron_ore and that is not switched off. Need per hour not measured: the runs record no goods used.

The Faction Fuel Bunker at our first outpost (system gsc_0044; the census names its station 443f0c5b2a1fbbcea95d13b76a797fe9): it holds up to 50,000 fuel, deposited from a docked ship's tank (catalog: faction_fuel_bunker, item fuel), and members refuel free from it. It held 0 on 2026-11-17 (Suggi). keep 5,000 is a first guess (Unity, 2026-11-17). The bunker is not in the storage book: its stock reads 0, not measured, until its reading is stored. Sources (Apollo, 2026-11-25 12:13 UTC): our own cells from Node Beta and cells bought at The Experiment, both gated below 5,000 by requires.reserve.

It read 0 at 12:04 UTC (empire.json faction_storage). keep 3,000: a first guess by Apollo, 2026-11-25 12:12 UTC (orders ENT-093 block APOLLO: a fuel supply-chain row with me); the draw is not measured yet.
